newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-L&G Australia moves to index-linking.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-L&G Australia moves to index-linking.

text.p: Legal and General Group (L&G) Plc's Australian unit said on Thursday it would manage a higher percentage of its funds in an index-linked way rather than trying to pick winning sectors or stocks.
L&G Australia managing director Derek Bullen told a news conference releasing the unit's annual sales figures that it had decided to aim for more consistent investment returns.
This meant L&G Australia would aim to increase its percentage of funds in index-linked funds from around 20 percent now to as much as 40 percent.
L&G Australia's investment performance for its various funds under management had not been as good as it should have been in recent years, Bullen said.
"We've tended to be in the third quartile," Bullen said, referring to the rankings of fund performance and adding he would like L&G Australia to aim for the second quartile.
L&G Australia's director of investment strategy John Stroud said the group had been burnt in 1994 by the bond market meltdown.

It was then hurt by the emerging markets selloff linked to the Mexican crisis in 1995 and had then been caught out by the split in fortunes between the resource and industrial sectors in Australia last year.
L&G Australia now aimed to be more consistent, he said.
Earlier L&G Australia announced that total new business rose 44.4 percent to A$615.3 million in calendar 1996.

This sharp rise was due in part to the unit's acquisition of SGIC from the South Australian state government and was helped by a A$161.5 million increase in funds invested in infrastructure bonds through L&G Australia.
